general.temas: The most frequently covered story is Jair Bolsonaro’s hospitalization, including the authorization for his children to visit him. Several outlets also cover the earthquake in Peru, cyberattacks on US government agencies and the death of executive Joe Wallach. Among the stories highlighted by just one newspaper is the clash between the PCC and Comando Vermelho on the border with Bolivia, in Gazeta do Povo.
general.motivo_crispacion: Tensions are moderate: fiscal adjustment is causing divisions within the government’s support base, as well as protests and criticism to which Lula has responded. In judicial matters, the charges against Congressman Marcel Van Hattem and Alexandre de Moraes’s decisions concerning the Bolsonaro family stand out. There are also clashes between criminal factions and an investigation into police violence against protesters in France. Health, culture, sports and science news provide a less contentious counterpoint.

Folha de S.Paulo.resumen:
- Taylor Swift says composing for “Toy Story 5” allowed her to move away from her autobiographical themes.
- One story explains that body odor arises when microorganisms on the skin metabolize substances in sweat.
- The front page covers Débora Nascimento’s return to soap operas and a review of the comedy “Sem Pai nem Mãe.”
- A man survived being stabbed in the neck in Minas Gerais; in politics, coverage includes plans for the New Year’s Eve celebration in Brasília and the Colombian president’s first 100 days.
- Also prominent are the death of executive Joe Wallach, an incident involving fans and bitcoin’s fall to its lowest level in more than two years.
Folha de S.Paulo.motivo_populismo: An informational tone predominates, although expressions such as “body bags,” “war on wokeness” and “overthrown” add drama; there is no apparent appeal to the people against the elites.
Folha de S.Paulo.sesgo: The selection devotes ample space to entertainment and combines news of incidents, politics and the economy with reviews and columns. The texts provided show no clear political orientation across the front page as a whole.

O Globo.resumen:
- The Brazilian government is preparing an official brand for the 2027 Women’s World Cup.
- A man was arrested in São Paulo for allegedly abusing three minors; in France, police officers are being investigated for violence and sexual assault against protesters.
- An earthquake in Peru injured at least 15 people; in Rio, high temperatures and possible storms are forecast.
- Bolsonaro remains in intensive care, stable and with no discharge date; another story covers research into erectile dysfunction drugs for Alzheimer’s.
- COP31 continues without consensus on fossil fuels; other prominent stories concern Joe Wallach, a wedding in Morocco and a swim to raise awareness of environmental damage.
O Globo.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly informational, although expressions such as “threat” and “one of the most disappointing summits” add drama; there is no apparent opposition between the people and the elites.
O Globo.sesgo: The selection gives space to incidents, weather, health and institutional affairs, alongside society news. No clear political orientation is apparent in the available text.

O Estado de S. Paulo.resumen:
- Corinthians loses a player to injury; Alcaraz reaches the ATP Finals final and Newcastle-Arsenal is announced.
- Bolsonaro remains in intensive care, stable and with no discharge date in sight.
- The FBI is investigating a possible cyberattack; US television networks report attacks on the FBI and the Department of Agriculture.
- Advice is offered on the 13th-month salary, statins and GTA 6.
- Also prominent are a family letter, comments by Iza and the relocation of a bookstore in São Paulo.
O Estado de S. Paulo.motivo_populismo: The tone is mostly informational, although “moves people” and the question “Do statins cause dementia?” seek to attract attention through emotion or concern, without framing a confrontation between the people and the elites.
O Estado de S. Paulo.sesgo: The selection prioritizes sports, service journalism and entertainment, alongside health and international news. No clear political bias is apparent in the headlines.

Gazeta do Povo.resumen:
- Bolsonaro receives hospital visitors under certain conditions; Father Kelmon will seek judicial authorization to attend to him.
- Decisions by Alexandre de Moraes affect Marcel Van Hattem and Flávio Bolsonaro; the Master case could reach the full Supreme Court.
- An assessment criticizes Lula’s economic record, while fiscal adjustment generates divisions and protests.
- Santa Catarina is planning a new industrial tender and assistance to restore historic houses.
- Also prominent are the clash between factions on the border with Bolivia, a sleep device and an intervention by Pope Leo XIV on technology.
Gazeta do Povo.motivo_populismo: An informational tone predominates, although expressions such as “stops delivering transformations” and the question “Goodbye insomnia?” introduce judgment and a degree of sensationalism, without a clear appeal to the people against the elites.
Gazeta do Povo.sesgo: The selection gives extensive attention to Bolsonaro and judicial decisions affecting his circle, alongside a critical assessment of Lula’s economic record. The approach combines political and judicial coverage with regional, religious, scientific and security news.

CartaCapital.resumen:
- A magnitude 6.7 earthquake injures 15 people in Peru.
- José Maria Neves is reelected president of Cape Verde.
- Bolsonaro remains hospitalized with an abdominal condition; Moraes authorizes daily visits by his children without cellphones.
- Rain affects more than 33 cities in Rio Grande do Sul; Lula promises federal support and responds to critics of his government.
- Prominent stories include the capture of a drug trafficker in Mexico, cyberattacks in the US and a South American volleyball title.
CartaCapital.motivo_populismo: Informational language predominates, although “devastated city” is a dramatic expression and a headline about Bolsonaro highlights an “imposed condition” to attract attention.
CartaCapital.sesgo: The front page devotes particular attention to Bolsonaro, his hospitalization and the decisions on visits, while also highlighting Lula’s actions and statements. The available headlines show no unequivocal political orientation.

opiniones.comunista:
I see a class contradiction at the heart of the news: while fiscal adjustment is being debated in Brazil, rain is battering cities in Rio Grande do Sul and forcing the mobilization of public teams. The solidarity announced by the government is necessary, but it is not enough: protecting the population requires permanent, funded public services capable of preventing and responding to disasters. I do not accept that the books should be balanced at the expense of those who live off their labor.

The lack of consensus at COP31 on fossil fuels also shows the limits of entrusting the green transition to the interests of big capital. I support collective ownership and democratic control of strategic sectors, including energy: decisions affecting the climate and employment must respond to shared needs, not private profit.
opiniones.anarquista:
COP31 remains without consensus on fossil fuels and climate finance. I do not trust a gathering of governments and parties to resolve on its own a crisis that requires changing who makes decisions about energy and for whose benefit. I believe communities and those who work in the sector should be able to organize the transition from the bottom up, with shared resources and open decision-making, without replacing one hierarchy with another.

The rain in Rio Grande do Sul and the earthquake in Peru also remind us that freedom does not mean living in isolation: we need mutual aid networks capable of responding to emergencies and sustaining themselves afterward. I do not reject aid to affected populations; I reject its dependence solely on orders from above. For me, solidarity is stronger when those who need it take part in deciding how it is organized.
opiniones.liberal:
I see a central issue in the debate over fiscal adjustment and the difficulties of controlling debt: the government cannot promise everything without demanding ever more from those who work and run businesses. I prefer a limited state that focuses its resources on essential functions, is accountable and allows taxes to be lowered sustainably. Fiscal discipline is not an accounting end in itself: it protects people’s freedom to decide how to use the fruits of their efforts.

Bitcoin’s fall is also a reminder that economic freedom entails personal responsibility. Investing involves risks, and no one should expect taxpayers to cover their losses. A free market needs clear rules and honesty, not a public guarantee that every bet will pay off.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I see a warning in the clash between the PCC and Comando Vermelho on the border with Bolivia: a country that does not control its territory gives up on protecting its citizens. I want guarded borders, cooperation against drug trafficking and strict control over who enters and remains in Brazil. Security is not prejudice: it is an obligation of the state.

I am also concerned that a priest was prevented from attending to Bolsonaro in the hospital. Without disregarding medical rules, I believe religious assistance deserves effective protection, especially in times of illness. And with COP31 lacking consensus on fossil fuels, I believe Brazil should determine its energy policy according to its own needs, not the priorities of international elites. Sovereignty means being able to choose, but also accepting responsibility for protecting our natural heritage and our traditions.
opiniones.centro:
Today I am concerned about two challenges that demand fewer slogans and more capacity to govern. COP31 remains without consensus on fossil fuels and climate finance. I believe a gradual transition, with verifiable targets and support for the countries that need it most, offers a stronger path than promising immediate changes without explaining how to fund them. The market can mobilize investment, but public rules and protection for affected workers are needed.

In Brazil, the rain in Rio Grande do Sul is a reminder of why we need institutions capable of acting when an emergency strikes. I welcome the federal mobilization and hope that aid will be coordinated with local authorities and that there will be accountability for its use. Fiscal responsibility matters precisely because a solvent state must be able to protect the population when it needs it most.
